title: Apple Wants to Charge Developers Up to 15 Percent for Linking Outside the App Store
excerpt: Apple today submitted a court-ordered proposal outlining the commission it believes is reasonable to collect from U.S. apps that link to purchase...
content_html:
Thursday August 13, 2026 3:11 pm PDT by Juli Clover

Apple today submitted a court-ordered proposal outlining the commission it believes is reasonable to collect from U.S. apps that link to purchase options outside of the App Store.


Apple is asking for half of its commission on standard apps, so apps that would pay 30 percent for an in-app purchase would pay 15 percent when linking to a web purchase option. Small Business Program participants that would normally pay 15 percent would pay 5 percent.

  • 15 percent - Standard apps.
  • 10 percent - Apps that are part of the News Partner Program, Video Partner Program, Mini Apps Partner Program, and subscription renewals.
  • 5 percent - Apps that qualify for the Small Business Program. Apps qualify if they earn under $1 million per year.

These proposed fees are what developers would pay when someone uses their app, taps a link in the app, and then makes a purchase on the website in the link. So if someone using the Spotify app clicked a link in the app to go to the Spotify website and then purchased a subscription, Spotify would owe Apple a 15 percent fee. Apple says the fees were calculated based on expert analysis, and they are lower than the link-out rates Google is charging in the Epic v. Google case.

Apple submitted the proposal to the U.S. District Court for the Northern District of California, where Judge Yvonne Gonzalez Rogers has been tasked with determining a reasonable fee for Apple to charge for its intellectual property.

The appeals court suggested the commission could be limited to the direct costs of facilitating link-outs, and under that approach, the fee would be zero. Apple says a zero commission would not reflect the value that it provides developers, and its suggested commission gives it fair compensation for the ‌App Store‌ platform.

As a recap, Apple was ordered to change its ‌App Store‌ rules to allow developers to link to purchase options outside of the ‌App Store‌ way back in 2021 during its legal dispute with Epic Games. Appeals delayed the ‌App Store‌ update for several years, but Apple eventually implemented a 12 to 27 percent fee that was nearly identical to its regular ‌App Store‌ fees when taking into account fees from third-party payment processors.

‌Epic Games‌ complained about Apple's fee structure, and Judge Gonzalez Rogers found Apple in contempt of court. In April 2025, she barred Apple from charging any fee on links, and since then, Apple has collected no money when an app sends users to a website to make a purchase. Apple appealed the ruling, and the appeals court upheld the contempt ruling, but said Apple was entitled to be compensated for its intellectual property. The appeals court sent the case back to the district court and Gonzalez Rogers to determine an appropriate fee.

With a loss on the contempt finding from the appeals court, Apple appealed to the Supreme Court. The justices agreed to hear the case in the term that starts in October. Apple tried several times to get the fee calculation paused until the Supreme Court rules on the case, but it was not successful.

The district court will now evaluate Apple's fee proposal and hear a response from ‌Epic Games‌, and Apple will need to implement the fee the court sets. Apple wanted to pause fee calculations because if the Supreme Court decides the appeals court erred when upholding the contempt ruling, it could nullify the district court's ruling barring Apple from charging fees.

content_html_zh:
太平洋夏令时间 2026 年 8 月 13 日星期四下午 3:11 作者：Juli Clover

苹果今天提交了一份法院下令的提案，概述了它认为从链接到 App Store 之外的购买选项的美国应用程序中收取的佣金是合理的。

苹果要求标准应用程序收取一半的佣金，因此为应用内购买支付 30% 费用的应用程序在链接到网络购买选项时将支付 15%。 通常支付 15% 的小型企业计划参与者将支付 5%。

  • 15% - 标准应用程序。
  • 10% - 属于新闻合作伙伴计划、视频合作伙伴计划、迷你应用合作伙伴计划和订阅续订的应用程序。
  • 5% - 符合小型企业计划资格的应用程序。 如果应用程序的年收入低于 100 万美元，则符合资格。

这些建议费用是当有人使用他们的应用程序、点击应用程序中的链接，然后在链接中的网站上进行购买时开发人员需要支付的费用。 因此，如果使用 Spotify 应用程序的用户点击应用程序中的链接访问 Spotify 网站，然后购买订阅，Spotify 将欠苹果 15% 的费用。 苹果公司表示，这些费用是根据专家分析计算得出的，并且低于谷歌在 Epic v. 案中收取的链接出费率。 谷歌案例。

苹果公司向美国加利福尼亚州北区地方法院提交了该提案，该法院法官伊冯·冈萨雷斯·罗杰斯的任务是确定苹果公司对其知识产权收取的合理费用。

上诉法院建议，该委员会可以仅限于促进链接的直接成本，根据这种方法，费用将为零。 苹果表示，零佣金并不能反映它为开发者提供的价值，其建议的佣金为其 App Store 平台提供了公平的补偿。

回顾一下，苹果在 2021 年与 Epic Games 发生法律纠纷期间被勒令更改其 App Store 规则，以允许开发者链接到 App Store 之外的购买选项。 上诉将“App Store”更新推迟了几年，但苹果最终收取了 12% 至 27% 的费用，在考虑到第三方支付处理商的费用后，该费用几乎与其常规“App Store”费用相同。

Epic Games 抱怨苹果的收费结构，冈萨雷斯·罗杰斯法官判定苹果藐视法庭。 2025 年 4 月，她禁止苹果公司对链接收取任何费用，从那时起，当应用程序将用户发送到网站进行购买时，苹果公司就不再收取任何费用。 苹果公司对裁决提出上诉，上诉法院维持了藐视法庭的裁决，但表示苹果公司有权因其知识产权获得赔偿。 上诉法院将案件发回地区法院，并由冈萨雷斯·罗杰斯确定适当的费用。

由于上诉法院藐视法庭的裁决败诉，苹果公司向最高法院提起上诉。 法官们同意在十月份开始的任期内审理此案。 苹果多次尝试暂停费用计算，直到最高法院对此案作出裁决，但没有成功。

地区法院现在将评估苹果的费用提案并听取“Epic Games”的回应，苹果将需要执行法院设定的费用。 苹果希望暂停费用计算，因为如果最高法院裁定上诉法院在维持藐视法庭裁决时犯了错误，则可能会使地方法院禁止苹果收取费用的裁决无效。
